competence_summary: Executes iterative 5-Why root cause drilldowns, grounding each causal inference in verifiable evidence (code, test, or process) to trace from immediate defect symptom down to root systemic failure.
reasoning_heuristics: Step 1 (Why 1 - Symptom): Why did the car rapidly unlock and lock repeatedly? -> Proximity state oscillated rapidly between True and False.
Step 2 (Why 2 - Code): Why did proximity state oscillate? -> proximity_controller.py checked a single threshold (distance <= 2.0) without a hysteresis deadband.
Step 3 (Why 3 - Design): Why was a single threshold implemented? -> Architectural specification REQ-004 omitted explicit hysteresis margin for noisy RF RSSI signal.
Step 4 (Why 4 - Testing): Why was this not caught in QA? -> Test suite tests/test_proximity_controller.py only evaluated static discrete points (1.0m, 3.0m) and omitted dynamic boundary jitter.
Step 5 (Why 5 - Process/Systemic): Why were boundary test cases omitted? -> Boundary test verification checklist was not enforced in CI pipeline for RF/sensor modules.
Step 6: Formulate systemic counter-measures for each validated Why layer.

candidate_agents.delegation_goal: Validate Why 2 code condition and AST logic.
Validate Why 3 specification omission in Neo4j.
Validate Why 4 test gap in QA suite.

input_guardrails: Initial problem statement must describe an observed defect symptom.
Must not accept circular or speculative reasoning without backing evidence envelopes.
safety_guardrails: ENG.ai must avoid assigning personal blame; focus on technical mechanisms and systemic processes.

pass_conditions: All 5 Why stages logically chained and evidenced.
Root cause grounded in deterministic technical facts.
Preventive counter-measures drafted for technical (Why 2) and process (Why 5) levels.

Each step has a bold 'Why' bubble with an associated evidence badge (Git icon, Neo4j icon, Test icon) in high-tech glowing cyan and purple palette.
